authority_boundary: Technique cards are bounded routing aids, not proof that ML is needed, that a technique will work, or that data use, training, deployment, or promotion is authorized. Local evidence and named humans decide adoption.
coverage_statement: This seed covers common ML problem families but is intentionally incomplete. Missing coverage stays unknown; the fortnightly research workflow may propose pointer-only additions after screening, evaluation design, and human review.

techniques.label: No-ML deterministic, statistical, search, or process baseline
applies_when: A proposed ML system needs a credible counterfactual.
Rules, search, ordinary statistics, optimization, or process repair may meet the goal.
does_not_apply_when: The task is itself a bounded study of a specific learning algorithm and makes no adoption claim.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: A weak straw baseline can make unnecessary complexity look valuable; rejecting ML without measuring the relevant outcome can also hide a useful opportunity.
data_assumptions: Baseline and ML candidate use equivalent permitted information at the same decision time.
split_and_leakage_controls: Evaluate on the same held-out units and time boundary as the ML candidate.
evaluation_requirements: compare outcome, failure cost, latency, maintenance, interpretability, and data risk
record cases where the simple option wins
techniques.authority_boundary: A baseline informs comparison only; it does not authorize production automation.

techniques.label: Linear and generalized linear models
applies_when: Relationships are adequately approximated by a specified link and feature representation.
Interpretability, calibration, latency, or limited data favors a simple model.
does_not_apply_when: Unmodeled interactions or nonlinear structure dominate and cannot be represented safely.
Coefficients would be misread as causal effects.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Misspecification, collinearity, leakage, extrapolation, or causal over-interpretation can produce confident but wrong conclusions.
data_assumptions: Training data represents the intended population and decision time.
Residual and link assumptions are checked for the chosen model family.
split_and_leakage_controls: Fit preprocessing and regularization inside training folds.
Use group or temporal splits when observations are dependent.
evaluation_requirements: task metric plus calibration for probabilistic outputs
techniques.authority_boundary: Model coefficients and predictions are candidate evidence, not causal, legal, medical, financial, or policy authority.

techniques.label: Decision trees, random forests, and gradient-boosted trees
applies_when: Structured data has nonlinearities or interactions that simple models miss.
A maintained tree implementation meets latency and deployment constraints.
does_not_apply_when: The data is primarily raw high-dimensional media without a suitable representation.
Small or shifted data cannot support the model complexity.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Overfitting, leakage, unstable feature importance, poor extrapolation, and uncalibrated probabilities can be mistaken for robust knowledge.
data_assumptions: Categorical and missing-value semantics match the chosen library.
Train and deployment feature distributions are monitored.
split_and_leakage_controls: Fit all encoders and resampling inside folds.
Use entity or temporal splits where rows share provenance.
For XGBoost categorical features, preserve category types and recoding semantics consistently across training, serialization, and inference.
evaluation_requirements: permutation or intervention-based explanations with limitations
when early stopping is used, bind inference to the reviewed best iteration and test serialization parity
techniques.authority_boundary: Feature importance and model scores are diagnostic candidates, not proof of cause, fairness, safety, or deployment readiness.

techniques.label: Imbalanced and cost-sensitive classification
end_goals: optimize decision value under rare outcomes
control precision recall or expected cost
applies_when: Class prevalence is low or error costs are materially asymmetric.
Thresholds and review capacity can be tied to operational costs.
does_not_apply_when: The positive class is undefined or labels are systematically missing.
Accuracy alone is the only available success criterion.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Resampling before splitting, prevalence drift, synthetic examples, or threshold tuning on the test set can create severe leakage and misleading performance.
data_assumptions: Observed labels and sampling permit estimation of the deployment prevalence or a correction plan.
split_and_leakage_controls: Resample only within training folds.
Preserve natural prevalence in validation and test data.
Group correlated events.
operational_requirements: safe default when scores are unavailable
techniques.authority_boundary: Rare-event scores route candidate attention only; high-impact actions require domain, fairness, privacy, and human gates.

techniques.label: Time-series forecasting
end_goals: forecast a future quantity with uncertainty
applies_when: The target, horizon, vintage, and decision time are explicit.
Historical patterns and exogenous inputs have defensible availability semantics.
does_not_apply_when: The future is dominated by unmodeled interventions or structural breaks with no scenario plan.
Random row splits would be used.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Look-ahead, revised historical data, overlapping horizons, regime change, and narrow point metrics can make a forecast appear reliable when it is not.
data_assumptions: Features are available at forecast origin.
Backtests cover relevant seasons and regimes.
split_and_leakage_controls: Use rolling or expanding-origin backtests.
Freeze data vintages and prevent horizon overlap leakage.
implementation_options: PyTorch for justified deep sequence models
techniques.authority_boundary: Forecasts are uncertain planning inputs; they do not authorize allocations or high-impact actions without accountable human policy.

techniques.label: Anomaly and novelty detection
applies_when: Normal behavior can be characterized and review feedback is available.
The output is treated as triage rather than proof of wrongdoing or defect.
does_not_apply_when: Normal behavior is highly multimodal or nonstationary without contextual modeling.
No one can review or act on alerts.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Anomaly can be confused with error, fraud, danger, or importance; uncontrolled thresholds can create alert floods and biased scrutiny.
data_assumptions: Training contamination and context shifts are assessed.
Distance or density representations are meaningful.
split_and_leakage_controls: Separate incidents or entities across evaluation.
Simulate plausible novel cases without leaking labels into representation fitting.
techniques.authority_boundary: Anomaly scores are review signals only and must never be treated as guilt, defect, threat, or priority without validated domain evidence.

techniques.label: Clustering and dimensionality reduction
applies_when: The representation and distance semantics are defensible.
Clusters remain candidate descriptions subject to stability and domain review.
does_not_apply_when: A discovered cluster would be treated as a natural or protected category.
Results are expected to provide causal or authoritative labels.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Scaling, distance, density, random seed, projection distortion, and forced cluster counts can create compelling but arbitrary group stories.
data_assumptions: The sample covers the intended population.
Missingness and high-dimensional geometry are addressed.
split_and_leakage_controls: Use held-out stability or bootstrap checks.
Do not fit a projection on future or unauthorized populations.
evaluation_requirements: reconstruction or neighborhood preservation as relevant
implementation_options: UMAP with explicit stochastic and distortion caveats
techniques.authority_boundary: Unsupervised structure is hypothesis evidence only; it cannot define people, policy, causality, or ground truth.

techniques.label: Learning to rank and recommendation
end_goals: improve relevance or utility under limited attention
applies_when: The ranking objective and exposure policy match downstream value.
Feedback bias, exploration, diversity, and cold-start behavior can be evaluated.
does_not_apply_when: Historical clicks or selections are treated as unbiased preference.
Ranking would silently determine rights or high-impact access.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Position bias, feedback loops, popularity lock-in, filter bubbles, proxy discrimination, and metric mismatch can amplify existing behavior rather than improve outcomes.
data_assumptions: Implicit feedback and missing-not-at-random behavior are modeled or bounded.
User item and time identities are split correctly.
split_and_leakage_controls: Split by time and user or session as deployment requires.
Prevent future interactions and duplicate items from leaking.
techniques.authority_boundary: Ranking scores allocate attention only under an explicit human policy; they do not prove merit, entitlement, truth, or safety.

techniques.label: Deep and self-supervised representation learning
problem_shapes: images audio text or multimodal inputs
applies_when: Data scale, modality, and task complexity justify learned representations.
A pretrained model or maintained architecture can be evaluated under local constraints.
does_not_apply_when: A small tabular problem is adequately solved by simpler models.
Compute, licensing, privacy, or reproducibility cannot be governed.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Shortcut learning, memorization, opaque failure modes, pretraining-data uncertainty, high compute, and spurious transfer can hide behind strong aggregate metrics.
data_assumptions: Training and pretraining distributions are relevant enough for the downstream task.
Augmentations preserve intended semantics.
split_and_leakage_controls: Deduplicate source entities and near-duplicates across splits.
Keep pretraining overlap and contamination unknowns explicit.
implementation_options: reviewed pretrained model with frozen or fine-tuned layers
techniques.authority_boundary: Representation quality and pretrained capability claims require local validation and do not transfer provider, dataset, or deployment authority.

techniques.label: Causal effect and uplift learning
end_goals: target interventions by expected incremental effect
applies_when: The intervention, outcome, timing, estimand, and identification assumptions are explicit.
Randomization or defensible observational identification is available.
does_not_apply_when: Predictive association is being substituted for causal identification.
Key confounders, interference, positivity, or treatment versions cannot be bounded.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Flexible learners cannot repair unidentified causal questions; hidden confounding, interference, selection, and post-treatment variables can reverse conclusions.
data_assumptions: Consistency, exchangeability or randomization, positivity, and interference assumptions are defended for the estimand.
split_and_leakage_controls: Keep post-treatment information out of features.
Use honest sample splitting or cross-fitting where required.
implementation_options: causal forests or doubly robust estimators with expert review
techniques.authority_boundary: Causal estimates remain assumption-bound evidence and never authorize treatment, policy, medical, legal, or financial action without qualified human review.

techniques.label: Online learning and contextual bandits
end_goals: optimize cumulative value under bounded exploration
applies_when: Actions produce timely measurable feedback and controlled exploration is ethically and operationally permitted.
Logging propensities and nonstationarity can be governed.
does_not_apply_when: Exploration can cause unacceptable harm or inequity.
Feedback is too delayed, confounded, or sparse for the proposed update rule.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Biased logs, missing propensities, unsafe exploration, nonstationarity, and reward misspecification can optimize the wrong behavior while reducing the evidence needed to detect it.
data_assumptions: Feedback corresponds to the chosen action and arrives within the learning horizon.
Context and action availability are logged.
split_and_leakage_controls: Use chronological replay with policy-aware estimators.
Do not evaluate a new policy from selectively logged outcomes without correction.
techniques.authority_boundary: Adaptive allocation requires explicit safety, fairness, experimentation, and human policy; reward optimization is not authority.

techniques.label: Reinforcement learning and sequential control
end_goals: optimize long-run reward under state transitions
learn policies in a validated environment
applies_when: Sequential actions materially affect future state and a high-fidelity simulator or safely bounded environment exists.
Reward, constraints, and off-policy risk can be reviewed.
does_not_apply_when: A supervised, planning, optimization, or bandit formulation is sufficient.
Real-world exploration is unsafe or the simulator is not decision-valid.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Reward hacking, simulator exploitation, unsafe exploration, distribution shift, irreproducibility, and long-tail failures can dominate apparent benchmark gains.
prerequisites: formal state action reward horizon and constraint contract
data_assumptions: Observed state is sufficient for the chosen formulation or partial observability is modeled.
Transition and reward behavior are stable enough or uncertainty is explicit.
split_and_leakage_controls: Separate training and evaluation seeds scenarios and environment variants.
Hold out adversarial and rare trajectories.
operational_requirements: hard safety constraints and kill switch
techniques.authority_boundary: RL policies are high-risk candidate controls and require simulation evidence, independent safety review, and explicit human deployment authority.

techniques.label: Graph and geometric machine learning
applies_when: Graph edges have defensible semantics and relational inductive bias matches the task.
Transductive versus inductive deployment is explicit.
does_not_apply_when: Edges are speculative, authority-laden, or generated similarity treated as truth.
A flat model captures the signal with lower complexity and leakage risk.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Graph construction leakage, homophily assumptions, oversmoothing, identity leakage, and generated edges can amplify false relationships or authority claims.
data_assumptions: Nodes and edges available at training and inference are distinguished.
Graph sampling preserves evaluation independence.
baseline_refs: label propagation with strict split controls
split_and_leakage_controls: Split by nodes edges time or whole graphs according to deployment.
Prevent message passing across held-out labels or future edges.
evaluation_requirements: shift to new nodes or graphs
implementation_options: scikit-learn baselines over reviewed graph features
techniques.authority_boundary: Graph relations and learned embeddings are candidate representations; they do not prove identity, cause, trust, importance, or governance authority.

techniques.label: Privacy-preserving and federated learning
applies_when: A formal privacy or data-locality requirement exists and the threat model is explicit.
Federated operations, secure aggregation, or differential privacy can be independently audited.
does_not_apply_when: Federation is used as a privacy slogan without a threat model.
The required utility privacy and operational tradeoff is unacceptable.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Gradients, updates, metadata, participation, or model outputs may leak information; federation adds attack surfaces and does not automatically provide privacy.
data_assumptions: Client heterogeneity participation and adversarial behavior are modeled.
Privacy accounting matches composition and release behavior.
split_and_leakage_controls: Separate clients sites or users across evaluation as deployment requires.
Audit update and output channels for membership and reconstruction risk.
evaluation_requirements: utility privacy security and communication tradeoff
operational_requirements: secure aggregation or trusted execution as specified
implementation_options: Flower or TensorFlow Federated with independent security design
techniques.authority_boundary: Privacy-preserving claims require formal parameters, threat-model evidence, and qualified privacy/security review; federation alone proves nothing.

techniques.label: Generative and multimodal learning
end_goals: combine text image audio or structured inputs
applies_when: The output is verifiable or reviewable and errors have bounded consequences.
Training or provider data, licensing, privacy, provenance, and safety constraints are understood.
does_not_apply_when: Unverifiable generation would become source truth or high-impact authority.
Copyright privacy security or safety review is unavailable.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Hallucination, memorization, prompt injection, unsafe synthesis, provenance loss, modality imbalance, benchmark contamination, and provider drift can produce persuasive but unsupported outputs.
prerequisites: output validation or human review contract
provider or model and data provenance
data_assumptions: Input modalities are aligned and permitted.
Generated outputs are labeled and never silently mixed with source observations.
split_and_leakage_controls: Deduplicate source and evaluation content.
Treat unknown pretraining overlap as a limitation.
Separate prompt and model selection from final test cases.
evaluation_requirements: safety privacy provenance cost and latency
operational_requirements: moderation or policy controls as applicable
implementation_options: reviewed open model and inference stack
techniques.authority_boundary: Generated output is candidate content only; it cannot become source truth, professional judgment, or deployment authority without verification and named-human gates.

techniques.label: Wide-and-deep and neural tabular learning
end_goals: combine memorized feature crosses with learned generalization
evaluate neural tabular representations against tree ensembles
applies_when: Sparse categorical interactions and nonlinear generalization are both material.
A linear or GBDT baseline leaves measured value and sufficient data and latency budget exist.
does_not_apply_when: A linear or boosted-tree model meets the decision goal.
Two-path complexity cannot be isolated with ablations.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Unbounded feature crosses, embedding leakage, weak baselines, and unnecessary two-tower complexity can create expensive apparent lift that does not survive shift.
data_assumptions: High-cardinality categories are stable enough to learn and unseen-category behavior is explicit.
Training volume supports the parameter count and deployment slices.
split_and_leakage_controls: Fit vocabulary embeddings crosses and preprocessing inside training folds.
Split by entity and time where interactions recur.
evaluation_requirements: held-out task calibration and slice metrics
latency memory model-size and unseen-category tests
operational_requirements: drift monitoring for category and interaction coverage
implementation_options: maintained tabular transformer after baseline evidence
techniques.authority_boundary: A wide-and-deep score is candidate prediction evidence, not confidence, cause, fairness, or deployment authority.

techniques.label: Frozen representations combined with tabular learners
problem_shapes: text image audio or graph context plus structured features
end_goals: reuse reviewed representations without end-to-end retraining
combine unstructured signal with strong tabular prediction
applies_when: A versioned encoder has defensible provenance and a frozen embedding can be evaluated independently.
The joined representation is available at prediction time and component lift can be ablated.
does_not_apply_when: Encoder data rights or evaluation overlap are unknown.
Tabular-only or representation-only baselines already meet the goal.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Unknown pretraining overlap, representation drift, join leakage, dimension-driven overfitting, and license loss can make a hybrid look stronger than it is.
data_assumptions: Representations align to the correct decision-time entity without future or duplicate leakage.
Embedding distribution can be monitored.
split_and_leakage_controls: Deduplicate raw source and encoder-evaluation overlap.
Create embeddings inside the permitted snapshot and split joins by entity or time.
implementation_options: frozen Hugging Face or approved encoder plus XGBoost
self-supervised encoder plus regularized linear model
techniques.authority_boundary: External or learned representations remain candidate features; they do not transfer source authority, licensing, or truth into DAD.

techniques.label: Calibration, quantile prediction, and conformal uncertainty
end_goals: produce empirically checked prediction sets or intervals
applies_when: Downstream decisions need probability or coverage semantics, not only rank order.
A calibration set exchangeability assumptions and rolling or slice coverage checks are defensible.
does_not_apply_when: Scores are used only for a fixed rank and no confidence claim is made.
Distribution shift invalidates the calibration contract and cannot be bounded.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: A nominal interval or calibrated aggregate can hide severe slice undercoverage, shift, adaptive reuse, or dependence violations.
data_assumptions: Calibration data resembles the stated deployment boundary or shift limitations are explicit.
Repeated entities and temporal dependence are handled.
baseline_refs: uncalibrated model reported honestly as a score
split_and_leakage_controls: Keep tuning calibration and final evaluation partitions distinct.
Use rolling or group-aware calibration for temporal or clustered data.
evaluation_requirements: reliability diagrams and proper scoring rules
coverage and width by slice and horizon
operational_requirements: monitor calibration and coverage when labels arrive
implementation_options: split conformal or conformalized quantile regression
techniques.authority_boundary: Calibration and conformal coverage are bounded statistical claims under stated conditions, not universal confidence or safety guarantees.

techniques.label: Active learning with calibrated uncertainty and diversity
end_goals: surface informative and diverse cases for governed review
applies_when: A human labeling loop has bounded capacity and reliable identity tracking.
Uncertainty diversity and random-sampling baselines can be evaluated without unsafe automation.
does_not_apply_when: Model uncertainty is uncalibrated or labels are not authoritative.
Selection feedback would silently redefine the target population.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Uncertainty sampling can chase outliers, amplify model blind spots, bias the labeled set, and create a feedback loop that looks like improvement.
data_assumptions: Candidate identities are stable and selection propensity can be recorded.
Human review quality and delay are measurable.
split_and_leakage_controls: Keep evaluation data outside the acquisition loop.
Track repeated entities and selection propensity across rounds.
implementation_options: modAL-style bounded loop after dependency review
custom deterministic queue with audited scores
techniques.authority_boundary: An acquisition score prioritizes candidate review only; it cannot label data, mutate source truth, or authorize downstream action.

techniques.label: Bounded AutoML and hyperparameter optimization
applies_when: The baseline split metric search space and compute budget are locked before search.
Nested evaluation or an untouched final test set prevents selection leakage.
does_not_apply_when: The target metric or split remains negotiable.
Search cost exceeds plausible decision value or encourages many unreviewed backends.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Repeated test access, metric hacking, search-space bias, nondeterministic pruning, and compute waste can turn optimization into overfitting.
data_assumptions: Trials share equivalent permitted data and preprocessing boundaries.
Parallel trials do not race on mutable artifacts.
split_and_leakage_controls: Run preprocessing and resampling inside trial folds.
Never optimize on the final untouched test set.
techniques.authority_boundary: Search optimizes only the locked candidate experiment; it cannot broaden tools, data, compute, metrics, or deployment authority.
